text:
Sam Torres: hey all — Sam here, first-day checklist. Trying to get parity across an M1 Mac and a small linux vm. Two odd things: 1) after running the dotfiles bootstrap my `~/.tool-versions` exists but `asdf current` shows system versions, not the ones listed. 2) brew installed asdf under /opt/homebrew but running `asdf plugin-add python` says permissions denied when creating plugin dir. I also use fish shell and the project's .envrc has `export VAR=value` which fish doesn't like. Any tips?

I ran:
```
brew install asdf direnv
git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/dotfiles.git ~/dotfiles
~/dotfiles/bootstrap.sh
# opened a new shell, ran asdf plugin-add python
```

Ivy (DevEx): welcome Sam! A few quick checks: first, `~/.tool-versions` only affects asdf when asdf is loaded and shims are in PATH. Make sure you source asdf before checking: in zsh/bash `source /opt/homebrew/opt/asdf/libexec/asdf.sh` and for fish use the sh-compat pattern: `set -gx ASDF_DIR $HOME/.asdf; . /opt/homebrew/opt/asdf/libexec/asdf.sh`. After that run `asdf reshim` and `asdf install`.

Permissions: Homebrew-installed asdf sometimes creates the plugin dir owned by root if you used `sudo` earlier. Check `ls -ld $(brew --prefix)/opt/asdf` and fix ownership: `sudo chown -R $(whoami) $(brew --prefix)/opt/asdf` or reinstall asdf via `git clone` into `~/.asdf` (we prefer that for per-user installs).

Fish + .envrc: fish doesn't accept `export VAR=val`. Either convert .envrc to POSIX style by running it under bash in direnv (`layout python` helpers) or in your fish config add a small shim to import exported vars, e.g.:
```
# ~/.config/fish/config.fish
function import_posix_env
  set -lx NM (mktemp)
  bash -lc "source ./.envrc && env > $NM"
  for line in (cat $NM)
    set -xl (string split '=' $line)[1] (string split '=' $line)[2]
  end
  rm $NM
end
```
But simpler: ask the repo owners to provide a `.envrc.fish` alternative or run `direnv allow` and let the project call a small bash wrapper.

Ben (Infra): also check that your project's `.tool-versions` isn't ignored in the bootstrap. Some bootstrap scripts copy a template into the repo root and require `git checkout` of the real `.tool-versions`. If you see the file but asdf ignores it, run `asdf local` in the repo to set it explicitly: `asdf local python 3.11.4` then `asdf install`.

Sam Torres: ah I had sourced asdf after opening a new shell but didn't add shims to PATH early. `set -gx PATH $HOME/.asdf/shims $PATH` in fish fixed seeing the tool versions. The plugin dir was owned by root (guess I used sudo earlier) — chown fixed it.

Ivy (DevEx): awesome. One more tip: we keep a `dotfiles/.tool-versions.example` and a helper script `scripts/apply-tool-versions.sh` that symlinks the repo file into place; if the bootstrap didn't run it you can run that script. Also file an issue on the dotfiles repo if the `.envrc` assumes bash-only — we like maintainers to include a fish-compatible snippet or a note.

Dotfiles Bot: canonical docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles (see scripts/ and docs/fish-compat.md). If anything still broken ping @dev-ex.

Sam Torres: thanks y'all — everything is green now on both machines. Leaving a small PR to add a fish-compatible .envrc note to the repo. :tada:
